claim_text: Spinodal decomposition: FluxNet-D at 1000*dt achieves 17.3x rollout speedup while preserving two-point correlation statistics.
blockers: No code repository URL appears anywhere in the paper text (searched for 'github', 'zenodo', 'anonymous.4open', 'code is available' -> zero hits).
No dataset URL or dataset-generation script is provided; all four benchmarks use simulation data generated by the authors with unpublished solver settings.

Reproducing the number requires full pushforward training (AdamW, K-step unroll) of both a ResNet and an FNO backbone plus 3-4 baselines, multi-seed, which is far outside an 8h CPU budget even if the data existed.

The speedup is defined relative to a GPU-accelerated explicit Cahn-Hilliard solver; no GPU is available in this environment, so the reference timing cannot be measured and the ratio is not defined on CPU.
Requires training three FluxNet-D models on 50k-step phase-field trajectories (t=2000..52000, snapshots every 10dt), data not released.
The two-point correlation metric S2bar(r) itself is implementable (FFT autocorrelation) but there is nothing trained to evaluate it on.
